name: Goldie
hook: A former graffiti artist whose 1994 label and 1995 album turned jungle's chopped, timestretched breaks into an art form, then talked David Bowie into making a drum and bass record.
blurb: Clifford Price, known as Goldie, grew up in foster care in the West Midlands before becoming a graffiti artist in the 1980s. In London in the early 1990s he moved into jungle production, pioneering timestretching on 'Terminator' (1992): stretching a drum break longer without changing its pitch, which let a six-second sample fill a whole track. He founded the label Metalheadz in 1994. His 1995 album 'Timeless' brought orchestral strings and soul vocals into jungle's chopped breakbeats, the genre's clearest bid for the ambition of a rock or classical record. David Bowie became a regular at Goldie's Metalheadz club night, and Goldie has said those nights directly inspired Bowie's own drum and bass album, 'Earthling' (1997), a rare case on this map of a rock legend's late reinvention running through a younger dance producer rather than the other way round. Bowie later returned the favour, singing on Goldie's 1998 album 'Saturnz Return'.
